chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Sayf ibn Amira, from one who mentioned him, from al-Harith ibn al-Mughira al-Nasri, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about the Word of God, Blessed and Exalted: 'Everything will perish except His Face' [28:88]. So he said: 'What are they saying about it?' I said: 'They are saying: Everything will perish except the Face of God.' So he said: 'Glory be to God! They have spoken a grievous word! Rather, He meant by that the Face of God which is the way that leads to Him.'

key_terms.تَبَارَكَ وَتَعَالَى: Blessed and Exalted — honorific formula for God emphasizing His transcendence
key_terms.سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ: Glory be to God — used here as an expression of disapproval at an incorrect theological statement
key_terms.قَوْلًا عَظِيمًا: A grievous word — indicating the seriousness of the anthropomorphic misinterpretation
key_terms.وَجْهَهُ: 'His Face/Countenance' — interpreted by the Imam not as a bodily attribute but as the path or means of approach to God

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the meaning of 'everything will perish except His Face' in Quran 28:88?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) was asked about the Quranic verse 28:88 — 'Everything will perish except His Face.' When told that people interpreted it as referring literally to God's face, he expressed strong disapproval, exclaiming 'Glory be to God!' He then clarified that 'the Face of God' in this verse refers to the way or path to God — i.e., the means through which one turns toward or approaches the Divine — not an anthropomorphic attribute. This interpretation reflects the Shia theological principle of tanzih (divine transcendence): God is beyond physical attributes, and such expressions in the Quran are to be understood metaphorically or as pointing to divine guidance and access.
